question: Does learned regime belief improve decisions when every arm uses the identical joint regime-fault planner?
scope: MTSK component and learned regime-posterior execution loop. Explicit addressing, regime catalogue, joint Bayes action/inspection updates and entity-local Bellman planning. Not full TAC-OSM, learned physics, CDL, CASM, selective computation, or a commercial validation.

generator.train: Half Markov with per-stream hazard uniformly selected .02,.08,.16,.32; half smooth/triangle drift, random phase, periods8,12,20,36,64. Both numeric endpoint ranges and waveform types seen in training.
generator.test: Switching hazards .04,.12,.24; smooth/triangle drift periods10,24,48; fresh streams. These interpolation changes do not establish arbitrary OOD robustness.
generator.observation: Same native known-fault repair coupons as DEV053B, public attempt and final verification only, cost1.2 each; fixture setup free. Probe outcomes never enter later prefixes. Distinct fresh stream seeds; native seed-index namespace used unchanged but no overlap with old streams.
generator.productive: Two entities, shared isolation slot, .85 noisy sensor, three repairs, four inspections, costs .1/1.2/4 for inspection/repair/residual fault. Same physical random world for each arm, full prefixes charged .6*N/entity.

joint: All arms supply a two-component posterior and rate table to exactly the same mixture_values/mixture_update planner. Marginal Beta represented by two identical rate vectors, hence no invented dependence. HMM uses train-labelled endpoint fit and calibration hazard. Neural softmax predicts next regime mixture from public history; endpoints fitted once from training labels, identically available to all arms. Conditional service consequences and inspection updates are explicit, not learned. Continuous drift is represented by soft endpoint weights and deliberately misspecifies endpoint-mixture uncertainty. Oracle uses two identical true current rate vectors. This tests posterior representation rather than new physical dynamics learning.

models.mtsk: Unmodified SwiLAMTSK d8 heads2 experts3 plus 5->8 encoder and 8->2 regime head; 1104 parameters, retained512B.
models.gru_matched: GRUCell input5 hidden15, nonlinear 15->6->2 head;1100 parameters, within1%; no padding or unused matching parameters.
models.gru128: GRUCell input5 hidden128, linear2 head; state-matched larger control, not an efficiency reference.
models.gru_hmm: Public HMM posterior appended to five public token features; GRUCell input7 hidden14, nonlinear14->8->2 head;1104 parameters plus explicit HMM state/operations, both reported.
models.mtsk_reset: Resets matrix and responsibilities before every observation in BOTH training and evaluation; separately retrained, same exposure.

training.loss: Soft cross entropy on next endpoint weight at all33 positions, derived from privileged training rates. Same targets available to HMM fit. Full BPTT; weights frozen at evaluation.
training.plateau: Report held-out validation cross-entropy change from768 to1024. Plateau diagnostic only if absolute relative improvement<=1%; no stopping, selection or extra training based on test outcomes. Lack of plateau limits conclusions.
training.failed_cells: Keep partial checkpoint and error, continue matrix; no post-test rescue or omission.

calibration.selection: Minimum expected repair Bernoulli log loss vs calibration next rates, all33 positions and3 actions. No native outcome selection. HMM features use selected hazard fixed before neural training.

metrics.primary: Absolute paired cost/entity difference vs stationary Beta, pooled equally across two families and three budgets. Also report each family/budget and costs against observations.
metrics.headroom: Fraction oracle gap closed secondary only where observed paired baseline-oracle gap>=0.05/entity AND fewer than1% of crossed bootstrap denominators<=0. Otherwise omit ratio and interval, retain absolute outcomes; inclusion rule frozen before outcomes. No selecting a population to manufacture primary success.
metrics.uncertainty: 5000 crossed paired bootstrap draws, whole stream cluster over budgets, globally resampled initialization seed, family stratified.256 independent evaluation streams, not768 seed-stream samples. Simultaneous Bonferroni95% intervals for4 MTSK contrasts vs GRUmatched, GRU128, GRU_HMM and reset.
metrics.reliability: No superiority claim unless adjusted upper cost contrast<0 vs matchedGRU and GRU_HMM, no additional aggregate residual faults or blocked/path violations for every seed/family, plus lower total cost on an explicitly measured deployment stream. This single-probe acquisition benchmark cannot establish commercial value.
metrics.economics: Per budget report .6*N acquisition/entity; optimistic break-even ceil(acquisition/(Beta-oracle cost)) when positive; model break-even only for positive observed savings. These are hypothetical repeated decision amortizations, not measured deployment ROI.
secondary: expected repair log loss and excess
fixed10-bin expected calibration error and Brier
inference timing including hybrid HMM filtering

audit: Separate process reconstructs every stream and checkpoint/calibration, exact tensor and prediction match, reruns decisions, independently replays each native primitive using existing separate accounting. Same author and shared model/generator code; development replay audit, not independent laboratory replication. Preserve original excluded split record and original archives.
budget: 15 fits x1024 updates and one deterministic reconstruction, bounded complete matrix, about30min process compute target; disclose actual runtime/overrun. Smoke three updates, disjoint namespace. No outcome-based stopping.
retrospective_DEV053: Separate review: verify reset retrained, Bonferroni adjustment for three memory comparisons and four registered guards; suppress unstable ratios in current review without changing original registered results; per-budget economics, calibration under shift. Old first/last-only logs cannot establish plateau. Treat DEV053B as null on adaptation. Parameter bytes are bytes, not parameter counts.
